conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes 'Yes' and cites strong randomized-trial evidence demonstrating that denosumab significantly reduces the risk of vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion:** Yes. Denosumab (Prolia) reduces the risk of vertebral fractures in osteoporosis, with strong randomized-trial evidence in postmenopausal women. In the pivotal 36-month FREEDOM trial, denosumab 60 mg given subcutaneously every six months significantly reduced vertebral (as well as nonvertebral and hip) fractures compared with placebo. A clinician guideline summarizes the vertebral-fracture reduction as approximately **68%** (reported at 1 year), with continued benefit in longer studies.

This evidence directly supports its use for postmenopausal osteoporosis in people at elevated fracture risk. The precise benefit for an individual depends on baseline fracture risk, age, prior fractures, bone density, and adherence to on-time dosing. Denosumab should not be delayed or stopped without a clinician-directed alternative treatment plan, because stopping can lead to rapid bone loss and increased vertebral-fracture risk.

Sources:  
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19671655/  
- https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493  
- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-021-05900-y  
- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11260113/
